title: Windows Vista Aero interface
lede: The desktop that gave the style half its name: tinted glass window frames over a green and blue aurora wallpaper.
summary: Glass window frames, a round Start orb, and an aurora wallpaper. Windows Vista, 2006–2007.
made: 2006 (released to manufacturing November 8, 2006; general release January 30, 2007)

evidence.note: Inspected the non-free 640 × 480 screenshot [File:Windows Vista.png](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Windows_Vista.png) (Windows Vista Ultimate with the Aero theme) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored. The operating system was not run.

styles.note: Windows Aero is the “Aero” in the style’s name, and scholars call Vista one of the first mature examples of the style.

context: Windows Aero is the design language introduced in Windows Vista in 2006 and continued in Windows 7. Its visual style emphasized “animation, glass, and translucency”; the name is a backronym for Authentic, Energetic, Reflective, and Open. [Wikipedia: Windows Aero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Aero).
Windows Vista was released to manufacturing on November 8, 2006, and internationally on January 30, 2007. [Wikipedia: Windows Vista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Vista).

Emirhan Avcı calls Vista’s Aero interface “one of the first mature examples of Frutiger Aero” and notes that Microsoft published an “Aero Aesthetics” guide for designers with Vista. [Avcı 2024, “Physical reflections of digital aesthetics”](https://doi.org/10.17932/IAU.EJNM.25480200.2024/ejnm_v8i3003), pp. 461–462.

The name Frutiger Aero joins the Frutiger typeface with Windows Aero. It was coined by Sofi Xian (then Sofi Lee) of the Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute in 2018. [Wikipedia: Frutiger Aero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frutiger_Aero); [CARI: Frutiger Aero](https://cari.institute/aesthetics/frutiger-aero).
observed: Window frames are translucent, blue-green tinted glass; the wallpaper shows through the title bar and borders.
The wallpaper is a dark green-to-teal field with luminous, curved light streaks, like an aurora.
The Start button is a round glossy orb at the bottom left; the taskbar is dark and glassy.
Sidebar gadgets on the right have rounded corners and soft shadows: an analog clock, a photo of a toucan, and a feed viewer.
Icons are detailed, shaded, and glossy (a globe, a padlock, a blue monitor).
interpretation: Vista is the reference point for the style’s surface grammar: glass instead of opaque chrome, light instead of line, and nature (aurora, toucan photo) placed inside a technical frame.
borrow: Use a thin, tinted translucent frame around content, with a lighter highlight along its top edge, rather than a solid title bar.
Place content on a dark-to-light luminous gradient with soft curved streaks instead of a flat background.
